subject: mathematics
question_text: Find the domain of the real function 1/((x² − 1)(x + 3)).

mark_split.label: Condition for the function to be defined

verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, Junior Inter Maths-1A (Sri Publishers, Machilipatnam), book p.81 — VSAQ chapter 14 Functions, question 98.1, on ★★★ SSP 81 (the book calls it 'the most dominating domain page'). Appearance years are printed board-split. UNLIKE the LAQ and SAQ pages, the book prints NO internal mark split on its VSAQ pages: the 1+1 across the two steps is our division of the 2 marks, not the source's. Publisher's claims until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms them.

recall_prompt: Say how you would find this domain — the condition the formula forces, and the answer.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Write the condition
steps.margin_note: One of the two marks is for the condition alone. Write it before any factorising.
steps.memory_tip: x² − 1 SPLITS as (x − 1)(x + 1), so there are three excluded points, not two.

recall.must_convey: That there is no square root here — the only rule is that the DENOMINATOR must not be zero.
accept: the denominator cannot be zero so x squared minus one into x plus three is not equal to zero
no root involved just set the denominator not equal to zero
factorise the denominator and say it is not zero
the only condition is that the bottom is non zero

steps.why: A rational function is defined everywhere its denominator is alive. Factorising x² − 1 is what reveals the second excluded point.
common_mistakes: Leaving x² − 1 unfactorised, so only x = −3 gets excluded.
Setting the denominator equal to zero and then giving THOSE values as the domain.

steps.label: Write the domain
steps.margin_note: The second mark is the answer set. Write it as R minus the three excluded points — this one is not an interval.
steps.memory_tip: R minus {1, −1, −3} — all three roots of the denominator.

recall.must_convey: That the domain is all real numbers except 1, minus 1 and minus 3 — all THREE excluded points.
accept: all real numbers except one minus one and minus three
R minus the set one minus one minus three
every real number except those three values
one minus one minus three thappa anni real numbers

steps.why: The answer is written as the whole real line with a finite set removed, not as intervals.
common_mistakes: Excluding only two of the three points, usually missing x = −1.
Writing the answer as an interval when it is R minus a set.

insider_note: Factorise x² − 1 before listing the excluded values, or −1 is quietly missed. Three points come out, so the domain is R − {1, −1, −3} and not an interval.
